questions.text: Let $A=\{-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}$. Let R be a relation on A defined by $xRy$ if and only if $0\le x^2+2y\le4$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in R and $m$ be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it a reflexive relation. Then $l+m$ is equal to

questions.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\log_e\left(\dfrac{2x-3}{5+4x}\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4+3x}{2-x}\right)$ is $[\alpha, \beta)$, then $\alpha^2+4\beta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Logarithm: $\dfrac{2x-3}{5+4x}>0$, so $x<-\dfrac54$ or $x>\dfrac32$.
Inverse sine: $|4+3x|\le|2-x|$, i.e. $(4+3x)^2-(2-x)^2\le0$, i.e. $(4x+2)(2x+6)\le0$, so $-3\le x\le-\dfrac12$.
Together: $x\in\left[-3,-\dfrac54\right)$, so $\alpha=-3$, $\beta=-\dfrac54$ and $\alpha^2+4\beta=9-5=4$.

questions.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of $x^2+\sqrt{3}x-16=0$, and $\gamma$ and $\delta$ be the roots of $x^2+3x-1=0$. If $P_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n$ and $Q_n=\gamma^n+\delta^n$, then $\dfrac{P_{25}+\sqrt{3}P_{24}}{2P_{23}}+\dfrac{Q_{25}-Q_{23}}{Q_{24}}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Each root of $x^2=-\sqrt3x+16$ satisfies $x^{n+2}=-\sqrt3x^{n+1}+16x^n$, so $P_{25}+\sqrt3P_{24}=16P_{23}$ and the first term is $8$.
Similarly $x^2=-3x+1$ gives $Q_{25}=-3Q_{24}+Q_{23}$, so $\dfrac{Q_{25}-Q_{23}}{Q_{24}}=-3$.
Sum $=8-3=5$.

questions.text: Let $A$ be a matrix of order $3\times3$ and $|A|=5$. If $\left|2\operatorname{adj}\left(3A\operatorname{adj}(2A)\right)\right|=2^{\alpha}\cdot3^{\beta}\cdot5^{\gamma}$, $\alpha, \beta, \gamma\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to
questions.sol:
For order 3, $\operatorname{adj}(2A)=4\operatorname{adj}A$, so $3A\operatorname{adj}(2A)=12A\operatorname{adj}A=12|A|I=60I$.
$\operatorname{adj}(60I)=60^2I=3600I$, and $2\times3600I=7200I$.
$|7200I|=7200^3=(2^5\cdot3^2\cdot5^2)^3=2^{15}\cdot3^6\cdot5^6$, so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=15+6+6=27$.

questions.text: The sum $1+3+11+25+45+71+\ldots$ upto 20 terms, is equal to
questions.sol:
The differences $2, 8, 14, 20, 26, \ldots$ form an A.P. with common difference 6, so $T_n$ is quadratic: $T_n=3n^2-7n+5$ (check: 1, 3, 11, 25).
$\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{20}T_n=3\cdot2870-7\cdot210+5\cdot20=8610-1470+100=7240$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{9}\left(\frac{r+3}{2^r}\right)\cdot{}^9C_r=\alpha\left(\frac32\right)^9-\beta$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbb{N}$, then $(\alpha+\beta)^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
With $x=\dfrac12$: $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{9}r\,{}^9C_rx^r=9x(1+x)^8=\frac92\left(\frac32\right)^8=3\left(\frac32\right)^9$.
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{9}3\,{}^9C_rx^r=3\left[\left(\frac32\right)^9-1\right]$.
Total $=6\left(\dfrac32\right)^9-3$, so $\alpha=6$, $\beta=3$ and $(\alpha+\beta)^2=81$.

questions.text: The sum of all rational terms in the expansion of $\left(2+\sqrt{3}\right)^8$ is
questions.sol:
The rational terms are those with even powers of $\sqrt3$, so their sum is $\dfrac{(2+\sqrt3)^8+(2-\sqrt3)^8}{2}$.
$a_n=(2+\sqrt3)^n+(2-\sqrt3)^n$ satisfies $a_n=4a_{n-1}-a_{n-2}$, $a_0=2$, $a_1=4$: $14, 52, 194, 724, 2702, 10084, 37634$.
Sum $=\dfrac{37634}{2}=18817$.

questions.text: The number of solutions of the equation $2x+3\tan x=\pi$, $x\in[-2\pi, 2\pi]-\left\{\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right\}$ is:
questions.sol:
Solve $\tan x=\dfrac{\pi-2x}{3}$: the right side is a decreasing line, $\tan x$ is increasing on each branch.
On each full branch $\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, $\tan x$ runs from $-\infty$ to $\infty$: one root each.
On $\left[-2\pi,-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, $\tan x$ rises from 0 to $\infty$ while the line stays between $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$: one root. On $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2},2\pi\right]$, $\tan x$ rises from $-\infty$ to 0 while the line stays between $-\pi$ and $-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$: one root.
Total $=5$.

questions.text: The radius of the smallest circle which touches the parabolas $y=x^2+2$ and $x=y^2+2$ is
questions.sol:
The parabolas are mirror images in $y=x$, so the shortest distance between them is twice the shortest distance from $y=x^2+2$ to $y=x$.
Distance of $(t, t^2+2)$ from $y=x$: $\dfrac{t^2-t+2}{\sqrt2}$, least at $t=\dfrac12$: $\dfrac{7}{4\sqrt2}$.
The smallest circle has this shortest distance $\dfrac{7}{2\sqrt2}$ as diameter, so $r=\dfrac{7}{4\sqrt2}=\dfrac{7\sqrt2}{8}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: A line passing through the point $P\left(\sqrt{5}, \sqrt{5}\right)$ intersects the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{36}+\dfrac{y^2}{25}=1$ at $A$ and $B$ such that $(PA)\cdot(PB)$ is maximum. Then $5\left(PA^2+PB^2\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Points on the line: $(\sqrt5+r\cos\theta, \sqrt5+r\sin\theta)$. Substituting, $PA\cdot PB=\dfrac{1-\frac{5}{36}-\frac{5}{25}}{\frac{\cos^2\theta}{36}+\frac{\sin^2\theta}{25}}=\dfrac{119/180}{\frac{\cos^2\theta}{36}+\frac{\sin^2\theta}{25}}$, largest when $\sin\theta=0$ (horizontal line).
Then $\dfrac{(\sqrt5+r)^2}{36}=1-\dfrac15$, so $\sqrt5+r=\pm\dfrac{12}{\sqrt5}$: $r=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt5}$ or $-\dfrac{17}{\sqrt5}$.
$PA^2+PB^2=\dfrac{49+289}{5}$, so $5(PA^2+PB^2)=338$.

questions.text: A line passes through the origin and makes equal angles with the positive coordinate axes. It intersects the lines $L_1: 2x+y+6=0$ and $L_2: 4x+2y-p=0$, $p>0$, at the points A and B, respectively. If $AB=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{2}}$ and the foot of the perpendicular from the point A on the line $L_2$ is M, then $\dfrac{AM}{BM}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The line is $y=x$. A: $3x+6=0$, so $A(-2,-2)$. B: $6x=p$, so $B\left(\dfrac p6,\dfrac p6\right)$.
$AB=\sqrt2\left|\dfrac p6+2\right|=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt2}$ gives $\dfrac p6=\dfrac52$, $p=15$.
$AM$ = distance of A from $4x+2y-15=0$ $=\dfrac{27}{2\sqrt5}$; $BM=\sqrt{AB^2-AM^2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{81}{2}-\dfrac{729}{20}}=\dfrac{9}{2\sqrt5}$.
$\dfrac{AM}{BM}=3$.

questions.text: Line $L_1$ passes through the point $(1, 2, 3)$ and is parallel to $z$-axis. Line $L_2$ passes through the point $(\lambda, 5, 6)$ and is parallel to $y$-axis. Let for $\lambda=\lambda_1, \lambda_2$, $\lambda_2<\lambda_1$, the shortest distance between the two lines be 3. Then the square of the distance of the point $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, 7)$ from the line $L_1$ is
questions.sol:
The directions are $\hat k$ and $\hat j$, with $\hat k\times\hat j=-\hat i$; the shortest distance is the $x$-separation $|\lambda-1|=3$, so $\lambda_1=4$, $\lambda_2=-2$.
$L_1$ is $x=1$, $y=2$. For the point $(4,-2,7)$: distance$^2=(4-1)^2+(-2-2)^2=25$.

questions.text: Let a line passing through the point $(4, 1, 0)$ intersect the line $L_1: \dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}$ at the point $A(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ and the line $L_2: x-6=y=-z+4$ at the point $B(a, b, c)$. Then $\begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\ \alpha&\beta&\gamma\\ a&b&c\end{vmatrix}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Take $A=(1+2t, 2+3t, 3+4t)$ and $B=(6+s, s, 4-s)$; with $P(4,1,0)$, $\overrightarrow{PA}=k\,\overrightarrow{PB}$:
$2t-3=k(2+s)$, $1+3t=k(s-1)$, $3+4t=k(4-s)$.
Subtracting the second from the first: $-t-4=3k$; adding the last two: $4+7t=3k$. So $t=-1$, $k=-1$, $s=3$.
$A=(-1,-1,-1)$, $B=(9,3,1)$; the determinant is $1(-1+3)-0+1(-3+9)=8$.

questions.text: If $y(x)=\begin{vmatrix}\sin x&\cos x&\sin x+\cos x+1\\ 27&28&27\\ 1&1&1\end{vmatrix}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+y$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Expanding along the first row: $y=\sin x(28-27)-\cos x(27-27)+(\sin x+\cos x+1)(27-28)=-\cos x-1$.
$y^{\prime\prime}=\cos x$, so $y^{\prime\prime}+y=-1$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}(1+ax)^{1/x}, & x<0\\ 1+b, & x=0\\ \dfrac{(x+4)^{1/2}-2}{(x+c)^{1/3}-2}, & x>0\end{cases}$ be continuous at $x=0$. Then $e^abc$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Left limit: $(1+ax)^{1/x}\to e^a$.
Right limit: the numerator tends to 0, so the denominator must too: $c^{1/3}=2$, $c=8$. Then the limit is $\dfrac{\frac{1}{2\cdot2}}{\frac{1}{3\cdot4}}=3$.
Continuity: $e^a=1+b=3$, so $b=2$ and $e^abc=3\times2\times8=48$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int x^3\sqrt{3-x^2}\,dx$. If $5f\left(\sqrt{2}\right)=-4$, then $f(1)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $u=3-x^2$, $x\,dx=-\dfrac{du}{2}$: $f=-\dfrac12\displaystyle\int(3-u)\sqrt u\,du=-u^{3/2}+\dfrac{u^{5/2}}{5}+C$.
At $x=\sqrt2$, $u=1$: $f=-\dfrac45+C$, and $5f=-4$ gives $C=0$.
At $x=1$, $u=2$: $f(1)=-2\sqrt2+\dfrac{4\sqrt2}{5}=-\dfrac{6\sqrt2}{5}$.

questions.text: Let $g$ be a differentiable function such that $\displaystyle\int_0^x g(t)\,dt=x-\int_0^x t\,g(t)\,dt$, $x\ge0$ and let $y=y(x)$ satisfy the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y\tan x=2(x+1)\sec x\,g(x)$, $x\in\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. If $y(0)=0$, then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Differentiating: $g(x)=1-xg(x)$, so $g(x)=\dfrac{1}{1+x}$ and the equation becomes $y^{\prime}-y\tan x=2\sec x$.
Integrating factor $\cos x$: $(y\cos x)^{\prime}=2$, so $y\cos x=2x$ (using $y(0)=0$).
$y\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)=\dfrac{2\pi/3}{1/2}=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$.

questions.text: If the number of seven-digit numbers, such that the sum of their digits is even, is $m\cdot n\cdot10^n$; $m, n\in\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
There are $9\times10^6$ seven-digit numbers. For any choice of the first six digits, exactly 5 of the 10 last digits make the sum even.
Count $=9\times10^5\times5=45\times10^5=9\cdot5\cdot10^5$, so $m=9$, $n=5$ and $m+n=14$.

questions.text:
All five letter words are made using all the letters A, B, C, D, E and arranged as in an English dictionary with serial numbers. Let the word at serial number $n$ be denoted by $W_n$. Let the probability $P(W_n)$ of choosing the word $W_n$ satisfy $P(W_n)=2P(W_{n-1})$, $n>1$.
If $P(\text{CDBEA})=\dfrac{2^{\alpha}}{2^{\beta}-1}$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to : __________
questions.sol:
There are $5!=120$ words, and $P(W_n)=2^{n-1}P(W_1)$ with $P(W_1)(1+2+\cdots+2^{119})=1$, so $P(W_n)=\dfrac{2^{n-1}}{2^{120}-1}$.
Rank of CDBEA: words starting A or B: 48; CA, CB: 12; CDA: 2; then CDBAE, CDBEA. So $n=64$.
$P=\dfrac{2^{63}}{2^{120}-1}$, so $\alpha+\beta=63+120=183$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the product of the focal distances of the point $\mathbf{P}\left(4, 2\sqrt{3}\right)$ on the hyperbola H: $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be 32. Let the length of the conjugate axis of H be $p$ and the length of its latus rectum be $q$. Then $p^2+q^2$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
Focal distances are $|ex\pm a|$, so their product is $e^2x^2-a^2=16e^2-a^2=32$, i.e. $16\dfrac{b^2}{a^2}-a^2=16$.
P lies on H: $\dfrac{16}{a^2}-\dfrac{12}{b^2}=1$. With $b^2=\dfrac{a^2(16+a^2)}{16}$ this gives $a^4=64$, so $a^2=8$, $b^2=12$.
$p=2b=4\sqrt3$, $p^2=48$; $q=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=6\sqrt2$, $q^2=72$; $p^2+q^2=120$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}=\lambda\hat{j}+\mu\hat{k}$ and $\hat{d}$ be a unit vector such that $\vec{a}\times\hat{d}=\vec{b}\times\hat{d}$ and $\vec{c}\cdot\hat{d}=1$. If $\vec{c}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{a}$, then $\left|3\lambda\hat{d}+\mu\vec{c}\right|^2$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
$(\vec a-\vec b)\times\hat d=\vec0$, so $\hat d=\pm\dfrac{-2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k}{3}$.
$\vec c\perp\vec a$: $\lambda+\mu=0$. $\vec c\cdot\hat d=\pm\dfrac{-\lambda+2\mu}{3}=\mp\lambda=1$.
With the + sign: $\lambda=-1$, $\mu=1$ and $3\lambda\hat d+\mu\vec c=(2\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k)+(-\hat j+\hat k)=2\hat i-\hat k$; the other sign gives the same vector.
$|2\hat i-\hat k|^2=5$.

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\max\{|x|, x|x-2|\}$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-2$ and $x=4$ is equal to __________
questions.sol:
For $x<0$, $x|x-2|<0$, so $y=-x$. On $[0,2]$, $x(2-x)\ge x$ when $x\le1$. For $x>2$, $x(x-2)\ge x$ when $x\ge3$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_{-2}^0(-x)dx+\int_0^1(2x-x^2)dx+\int_1^3x\,dx+\int_3^4(x^2-2x)dx=2+\frac23+4+\frac{16}{3}=12$.

questions.text: A person measures mass of 3 different particles as 435.42 g, 226.3 g and 0.125 g. According to the rules for arithmetic operations with significant figures, the addition of the masses of 3 particles will be.
questions.sol:
In addition the result keeps as many decimal places as the least precise term; 226.3 g has one decimal place.
$435.42+226.3+0.125=661.845$ g, rounded to one decimal place: 661.8 g.

Match the LIST-I with LIST-II

questions.text: A particle is released from height S above the surface of the earth. At certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of the earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively.
questions.sol:
Taking potential energy $mgh$ from the surface, energy is conserved: $mgS=K+U=4U=4mgh$, so $h=\dfrac S4$.
$\dfrac12mv^2=3mgh=\dfrac34mgS$, so $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{3gS}{2}}$.

questions.text: The angle of projection of a particle is measured from the vertical axis as $\phi$ and the maximum height reached by the particle is $h_m$. Here $h_m$ as function of $\phi$ can be presented as
questions.note: With the angle measured from the vertical, $h_m=\dfrac{u^2\cos^2\phi}{2g}$. Its graph starts flat at the maximum at $\phi=0$ and falls to zero at $90^\circ$ (strictly with zero slope there as well). NTA's final key gives graph (3), the curve that is greatest at $\phi=0$, flat there and falls to zero at $90^\circ$.
questions.sol:
The vertical component of velocity is $u\cos\phi$, so $h_m=\dfrac{u^2\cos^2\phi}{2g}$.
$h_m$ is greatest at $\phi=0$ with zero slope there, decreases as $\phi$ grows and becomes zero at $\phi=90^\circ$.
Of the four sketches, graph (3) shows this behaviour.

questions.text:
Which of the following curves possibly represent one-dimensional motion of a particle?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: phase increasing linearly with time describes simple harmonic motion: possible.
B: a closed velocity-displacement curve (an ellipse, here drawn as a circle with suitable scales) is also simple harmonic motion: possible.
C: a circle on a velocity-time graph would give two velocities at the same instant: impossible.
D: total distance never decreases with time: possible. Hence A, B and D.

questions.text: A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20 kg, kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is
questions.sol:
Let friction $f$ act forwards at the contact point. $F+f=ma$ and, about the centre, $(F-f)R=\dfrac25mR^2\cdot\dfrac aR$.
Adding: $2F=\dfrac75ma$, so $a=\dfrac{10F}{7m}=\dfrac{10\times49}{7\times20}=3.5$ m/s$^2$.

questions.text:
Consider a completely full cylindrical water tank of height 1.6 m and of cross-sectional area 0.5 m$^2$. It has a small hole in its side at a height 90 cm from the bottom. Assume, the cross-sectional area of the hole to be negligibly small as compared to that of the water tank. If a load 50 kg is applied at the top surface of the water in the tank then the velocity of the water coming out at the instant when the hole is opened is:
($g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Depth of the hole below the surface: $1.6-0.9=0.7$ m. Extra pressure from the load: $\dfrac{50\times10}{0.5}=1000$ Pa.
Bernoulli: $\dfrac12\rho v^2=\rho gh+\Delta p$, so $v^2=2(10\times0.7)+\dfrac{2\times1000}{1000}=16$.
$v=4$ m/s.

questions.text: During the melting of a slab of ice at 273 K at atmospheric pressure:
options: Positive work is done on the ice-water system by the atmosphere.
Positive work is done by the ice-water system on the atmosphere.
Internal energy of ice-water system remains unchanged.
Internal energy of the ice-water system decreases.
questions.sol:
Ice contracts on melting, so the atmosphere pushes in on the system: positive work is done on it by the atmosphere.
Latent heat is absorbed while the volume falls, so the internal energy increases.

questions.text:
A gas is kept in a container having walls which are thermally non-conducting. Initially the gas has a volume of 800 cm$^3$ and temperature 27$^\circ$C. The change in temperature when the gas is adiabatically compressed to 200 cm$^3$ is:
(Take $\gamma=1.5$ ; $\gamma$ is the ratio of specific heats at constant pressure and at constant volume)
questions.sol:
Adiabatic: $TV^{\gamma-1}=$ constant, so $T_2=300\left(\dfrac{800}{200}\right)^{0.5}=600$ K.
Change in temperature $=600-300=300$ K.

questions.text: A piston of mass M is hung from a massless spring whose restoring force law goes as $F=-kx^3$, where k is the spring constant of appropriate dimension. The piston separates the vertical chamber into two parts, where the bottom part is filled with 'n' moles of an ideal gas. An external work is done on the gas isothermally (at a constant temperature T) with the help of a heating filament (with negligible volume) mounted in lower part of the chamber, so that the piston goes up from a height $L_0$ to $L_1$, the total energy delivered by the filament is :(Assume spring to be in its natural length before heating)
questions.note: NTA's final key gives option (2). Strictly, a spring at its natural length when the piston is at $L_0$ stores $\dfrac k4(L_1-L_0)^4$ when the piston reaches $L_1$, not $\dfrac k4\left(L_1^4-L_0^4\right)$; the key's expression treats the spring deformation as the height itself.
questions.sol:
The gas expands isothermally, so the work it does is $nRT\ln\dfrac{V_1}{V_0}=nRT\ln\dfrac{L_1}{L_0}$.
The piston gains potential energy $Mg(L_1-L_0)$, and the spring (force $kx^3$) stores $\displaystyle\int kx^3\,dx=\frac k4x^4$, taken between the limits $L_0$ and $L_1$ in the intended answer.
Adding these gives option (2).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Two blocks of masses m and M, $(M>m)$, are placed on a frictionless table as shown in figure. A massless spring with spring constant k is attached with the lower block. If the system is slightly displaced and released, then
($\mu$ = coefficient of friction between the two blocks)
A. The time period of small oscillation of the two blocks is $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{(m+M)}{k}}$
B. The acceleration of the blocks is $a=-\dfrac{kx}{M+m}$
($x$ = displacement of the blocks from the mean position)
C. The magnitude of the frictional force on the upper block is $\dfrac{m\mu|x|}{M+m}$
D. The maximum amplitude of the upper block, if it does not slip, is $\dfrac{\mu(M+m)g}{k}$
E. Maximum frictional force can be $\mu(M+m)g$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Moving together, the blocks form a mass $M+m$ on the spring: $a=-\dfrac{kx}{M+m}$ and $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{M+m}{k}}$ (A, B true).
Friction on the upper block supplies its acceleration: $f=\dfrac{mk|x|}{M+m}$, not $\dfrac{m\mu|x|}{M+m}$ (C false).
No slipping needs $\dfrac{mkA}{M+m}\le\mu mg$, so $A_{max}=\dfrac{\mu(M+m)g}{k}$ (D true); the largest friction is $\mu mg$ (E false).

questions.text: A wire of length 25 m and cross-sectional area 5 mm$^2$ having resistivity of $2\times10^{-6}\ \Omega$ m is bent into a complete circle. The resistance between diametrically opposite points will be
questions.note: Dropped in NTA's final key (full marks to all candidates): the correct value, 2.5 $\Omega$, is not among the options. The answer marked here is only a placeholder.
questions.sol:
$R=\dfrac{\rho l}{A}=\dfrac{2\times10^{-6}\times25}{5\times10^{-6}}=10\ \Omega$.
Between diametrically opposite points the two halves (5 $\Omega$ each) are in parallel: $2.5\ \Omega$, which is not among the options.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor is filled equally(half) with two dielectrics of dielectric constants $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$, as shown in figures. The distance between the plates is d and area of each plate is A. If capacitance in first configuration and second configuration are $C_1$ and $C_2$ respectively, then $\dfrac{C_1}{C_2}$ is :
questions.sol:
First configuration: two layers of thickness $\dfrac d2$ in series: $C_1=\dfrac{2\varepsilon_0A}{d}\cdot\dfrac{\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2}{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2}$.
Second configuration: two halves of area $\dfrac A2$ in parallel: $C_2=\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2)}{2d}$.
$\dfrac{C_1}{C_2}=\dfrac{4\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2}{(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2)^2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The electrostatic potential on the surface of uniformly charged spherical shell of radius R = 10 cm is 120 V. The potential at the centre of shell, at a distance r = 5 cm from centre, and at a distance r = 15 cm from the centre of the shell respectively, are:
questions.sol:
Inside a charged shell the field is zero, so the potential everywhere inside equals the surface value: 120 V at the centre and at 5 cm.
Outside, $V\propto\dfrac1r$: at 15 cm, $V=120\times\dfrac{10}{15}=80$ V.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The radiation pressure exerted by a 450 W light source on a perfectly reflecting surface placed at 2m away from it, is
questions.sol:
Intensity at 2 m: $I=\dfrac{450}{4\pi(2)^2}\approx8.95$ W/m$^2$.
For a perfect reflector $p=\dfrac{2I}{c}=\dfrac{2\times8.95}{3\times10^8}\approx6\times10^{-8}$ Pa.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider following statements for refraction of light through prism, when angle of deviation is minimum.
A. The refracted ray inside prism becomes parallel to the base.
B. Larger angle prisms provide smaller angle of minimum deviation.
C. Angle of incidence and angle of emergence becomes equal.
D. There are always two sets of angle of incidence for which deviation will be same except at minimum deviation setting.
E. Angle of refraction becomes double of prism angle.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
At minimum deviation the path is symmetric: $i=e$ (C) and the ray inside runs parallel to the base (A, for the usual isosceles prism).
Any other deviation occurs for two angles of incidence, which swap with the emergence angle (D).
A larger prism angle gives a larger minimum deviation (B false), and $r=\dfrac A2$, not $2A$ (E false).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The radii of curvature for a thin convex lens are 10 cm and 15 cm respectively. The focal length of the lens is 12 cm. The refractive index of the lens material is
questions.sol:
Lens maker's formula for a biconvex lens: $\dfrac1{12}=(\mu-1)\left(\dfrac1{10}+\dfrac1{15}\right)=\dfrac{\mu-1}{6}$.
$\mu-1=0.5$, so $\mu=1.5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The work function of a metal is 3 eV. The color of the visible light that is required to cause emission of photoelectrons is
questions.sol:
Threshold wavelength $\lambda_0=\dfrac{hc}{\phi}=\dfrac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{3\text{ eV}}\approx413$ nm.
Only light of shorter wavelength (higher frequency) can emit electrons; of the given colours only blue is near this end of the spectrum.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-ILIST-II
A. $\mathrm{{}_0^1n+{}_{92}^{235}U\rightarrow{}_{54}^{140}Xe+{}_{38}^{94}Sr+2\,{}_0^1n}$I. Chemical reaction
B. $\mathrm{2H_2+O_2\rightarrow2H_2O}$II. Fusion with +ve Q value
C. $\mathrm{{}_1^2H+{}_1^2H\rightarrow{}_2^3He+{}_0^1n}$III. Fission
D. $\mathrm{{}_1^1H+{}_1^3H\rightarrow{}_1^2H+{}_1^2H}$IV. Fusion with -ve Q value
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: a heavy nucleus splits after neutron capture: fission (III). B: only electrons rearrange: chemical reaction (I).
C: two deuterons join to give helium-3: fusion releasing energy (II).
D: the binding energy of two deuterons ($2\times2.22$ MeV) is less than that of $\mathrm{^3H}$ (8.48 MeV), so energy must be supplied: negative Q (IV).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Choose the correct logic circuit for the given truth table having inputs A and B.
InputsOutput
ABY
000
010
101
111
questions.sol:
The table shows $Y=A$.
Circuit (4) feeds A and $A+B$ (OR output) into an AND gate: $Y=A\cdot(A+B)=A$.
Circuit (1) gives $\bar A(A+B)=\bar AB$, circuit (2) gives $B(A+B)=B$ and circuit (3) gives $A\cdot\overline{A+B}=0$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Three identical spheres of mass m, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of length $a$. When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time T = 4 seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length $2a$ and also the masses of the spheres are made 2m, then they will collide after __________ seconds.
questions.sol:
The only quantities are $G$, $m$ and $a$, so by dimensions $T\propto\sqrt{\dfrac{a^3}{Gm}}$.
New time: $4\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{2}}=8$ s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A 4.0 cm long straight wire carrying a current of 8A is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.15 T. The magnetic force on the wire is __________ mN.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A loop ABCDA, carrying current I = 12 A, is placed in a plane, consists of two semi-circular segments of radius $R_1=6\pi$ m and $R_2=4\pi$ m. The magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at center O is $k\times10^{-7}$ T. The value of k is __________.
(Given $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T m A$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
The straight parts AB and CD point along O and give no field. The current goes round the two semicircles in opposite senses, so their fields oppose.
$B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4}\left(\dfrac1{R_2}-\dfrac1{R_1}\right)=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times12}{4}\left(\dfrac1{4\pi}-\dfrac1{6\pi}\right)=12\pi\times10^{-7}\times\dfrac{1}{12\pi}=1\times10^{-7}$ T.
$k=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In the figure shown below, a resistance of 150.4 $\Omega$ is connected in series to an ammeter A of resistance 240 $\Omega$. A shunt resistance of 10 $\Omega$ is connected in parallel with the ammeter. The reading of the ammeter is __________ mA.
questions.sol:
Ammeter with shunt: $\dfrac{240\times10}{250}=9.6\ \Omega$; total resistance $150.4+9.6=160\ \Omega$.
Main current $=\dfrac{20}{160}=0.125$ A. The ammeter takes the fraction $\dfrac{10}{250}$: $0.125\times\dfrac{10}{250}=0.005$ A $=5$ mA.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities 4I and 9I are superimposed. The difference between the maximum and minimum intensities in the resulting interference pattern is $x$I. The value of $x$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$I_{max}=(\sqrt{4I}+\sqrt{9I})^2=25I$ and $I_{min}=(\sqrt{9I}-\sqrt{4I})^2=I$.
Difference $=24I$, so $x=24$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Among $10^{-9}$ g (each) of the following elements, which one will have the highest number of atoms?
Element: Pb, Po, Pr and Pt
questions.sol:
For equal masses the number of atoms is inversely proportional to the atomic mass.
Atomic masses: Pr $\approx141$, Pt $\approx195$, Pb $\approx207$, Po $\approx209$. Pr is lightest, so it has the most atoms.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following postulate of Bohr's model of hydrogen atom is not in agreement with quantum mechanical model of an atom?
options: An atom can take only certain distinct energies $E_1$, $E_2$, $E_3$, etc. These allowed states of constant energy are called the stationary states of atom.
An atom in a stationary state does not emit electromagnetic radiation as long as it stays in the same state.
When an electron makes a transition from a higher energy stationary state to a lower energy stationary state, then it emits a photon of light.
The electron in a H atom's stationary state moves in a circle around the nucleus.
questions.sol:
Quantised energies, no radiation from a stationary state and photon emission on a downward transition all survive in quantum mechanics.
A definite circular path does not: by the uncertainty principle an electron has no well-defined trajectory, only a probability distribution (orbital).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following properties will change when system containing solution 1 will become solution 2?
questions.sol:
Solution 1 has 1 mol of x per litre of water. Solution 2 has (1 + 1) mol of x in (1 + 1) L of water: the same composition, but twice the amount.
Intensive properties (molar heat capacity, density, concentration) are unchanged; Gibbs free energy is extensive, so it changes.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
2 moles each of ethylene glycol and glucose are dissolved in 500 g of water. The boiling point of the resulting solution is:
(Given : Ebullioscopic constant of water = 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$)
questions.sol:
Both solutes are non-electrolytes: total 4 mol in 0.5 kg, molality 8 mol kg$^{-1}$.
$\Delta T_b=0.52\times8=4.16$ K, so $T_b=373.15+4.16\approx377.3$ K.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In the following system, $\mathrm{PCl_5(g)\rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g)+Cl_2(g)}$ at equilibrium, upon addition of xenon gas at constant T & p, the concentration of
questions.note: NTA's final key gives option (1). Adding an inert gas at constant pressure increases the volume, and the equilibrium shifts forward, so the amounts (moles) of $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ increase. Strictly, their molar concentrations still fall: if $[\mathrm{PCl_3}]=[\mathrm{Cl_2}]$ rose, $K_c$ would require $[\mathrm{PCl_5}]$ to rise too, which is impossible. Option (2) would then also be true. The key has been followed.
questions.sol:
At constant T and p the inert gas increases the volume, which lowers the partial pressures of all three gases.
The reaction has more gaseous moles on the right, so the equilibrium shifts forwards and more $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ are formed.
NTA's key reads this as an increase in $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ (see the note).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Correct order of limiting molar conductivity for cations in water at 298 K is :
questions.sol:
Limiting molar conductivities (S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, 298 K): $\mathrm{H^+}$ 349.6, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ 119.0, $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ 106.0, $\mathrm{K^+}$ 73.5, $\mathrm{Na^+}$ 50.1.
Order: $\mathrm{H^+>Ca^{2+}>Mg^{2+}>K^+>Na^+}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : A catalyst cannot alter the equilibrium constant $(K_c)$ of the reaction, temperature remaining constant.
Statement II : A homogenous catalyst can change the equilibrium composition of a system, temperature remaining constant.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
A catalyst speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally, so $K_c$ (at fixed temperature) is unchanged: I is true.
For the same reason no catalyst, homogeneous or not, changes the equilibrium composition; it only shortens the time to reach it: II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In a reaction $\mathrm{A+B\rightarrow C}$, initial concentrations of A and B are related as $[\mathrm{A}]_0=8[\mathrm{B}]_0$. The half lives of A and B are 10 min and 40 min, respectively. If they start to disappear at the same time, both following first order kinetics, after how much time will the concentration of both the reactants be same ?
questions.sol:
$[\mathrm A]=8[\mathrm B]_0\cdot2^{-t/10}$ and $[\mathrm B]=[\mathrm B]_0\cdot2^{-t/40}$.
Equal when $2^3=2^{t/10-t/40}=2^{3t/40}$, so $t=40$ min.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I
(Molecules/ ion)		LIST-II
(Hybridisation of central atom)
A. $\mathrm{PF_5}$I. $dsp^2$
B. $\mathrm{SF_6}$II. $sp^3d$
C. $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$III. $sp^3d^2$
D. $\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}}$IV. $sp^3$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{PF_5}$: 5 bond pairs, trigonal bipyramidal, $sp^3d$ (II). $\mathrm{SF_6}$: octahedral, $sp^3d^2$ (III).
$\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$: Ni(0), tetrahedral, $sp^3$ (IV). $\mathrm{[PtCl_4]^{2-}}$: Pt(II), $d^8$, square planar, $dsp^2$ (I).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. The process of adding an electron to a neutral gaseous atom is always exothermic.
B. The process of removing an electron from an isolated gaseous atom is always endothermic.
C. The 1$^{\text{st}}$ ionization energy of boron is less than that of beryllium.
D. The electronegativity of C is 2.5 in $\mathrm{CH_4}$ and $\mathrm{CCl_4}$
E. Li is the most electropositive among elements of group I.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: false; adding an electron to atoms such as the noble gases (or N, Be) needs energy.
B: true; ionisation always needs energy. C: true; boron loses a $2p$ electron, which is easier to remove than beryllium's $2s$ electron.
D: false; electronegativity depends on the atom's environment (oxidation state, hybridisation), so it is not the same in $\mathrm{CH_4}$ and $\mathrm{CCl_4}$. E: false; electropositive character increases down the group (Cs, Fr).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : The N - N single bond is weaker and longer than that of P - P single bond.
Statement II : Compounds of group 15 elements in + 3 oxidation states readily undergo disproportionation reactions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
I: the N-N single bond is weaker than P-P (repulsion between lone pairs on the small N atoms), but it is shorter, not longer: false.
II: the +3 state becomes more stable down the group (inert pair effect); compounds of the heavier elements in +3 do not readily disproportionate, so the general statement is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The metal ions that have the calculated spin-only magnetic moment value of 4.9 B.M. are :
A. $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$
B. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$
C. $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$
D. $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$
E. $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=4.9$ B.M. means $n=4$ unpaired electrons.
$\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ ($d^4$), $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ($d^6$) and $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ ($d^4$) have 4; $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ ($d^5$) has 5 and $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ ($d^7$) has 3.
Hence A, B and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of the complexes $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(H_2O)]^{3+}}$ (A), $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ (B), $\mathrm{[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ (C) and $\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_3)_5]^{2+}}$ (D) in terms of wavelength of light absorbed is
questions.sol:
All are Co(III) complexes; the splitting $\Delta_o$ follows the spectrochemical series $\mathrm{CN^->NH_3>H_2O>Cl^-}$, so $\Delta_o$: C > B > A > D.
The wavelength absorbed varies inversely with $\Delta_o$: D > A > B > C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements from the following.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: pentan-3-one and pentan-2-one have different alkyl groups on either side of the C=O group: metamers (true).
B: a nitrile ($-\mathrm{CN}$) and an isocyanide ($-\mathrm{NC}$) with the same formula: functional isomers (true).
C: the two alcohols do not differ only in the position of the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group on the same carbon chain, so they are not position isomers (false).
D: a primary amine and a secondary amine belong to different classes, so they are not members of one homologous series (false). Hence A and B.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Which compound would give 3-methyl-6-oxoheptanal upon ozonolysis?
questions.sol:
3-Methyl-6-oxoheptanal is $\mathrm{OHC{-}CH_2{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CO{-}CH_3}$: both carbonyl carbons came from one ring C=C.
Joining C1 (CHO) and C6 (C=O) back together gives a cyclohexene with a methyl on the alkene carbon (C6) and another on the carbon three positions round from it (C3): 1,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene.
That is option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify [A], [B] and [C], respectively in the following reaction sequence:
questions.sol:
Benzenediazonium chloride is made from aniline with $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$/HCl at 273-278 K, so A is aniline.
KI replaces the diazonium group by iodine: B is iodobenzene.
2Na in dry ether (Fittig reaction) couples two aryl groups: C is biphenyl.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The least acidic compound, among the following is:
questions.sol:
Benzenesulphonic acid (B) is a strong acid, propanoic acid (C) has p$K_a\approx4.9$ and 3-ethoxyphenol (A) about 10.
The acetylenic C-H of ethyl propiolate (D) is far weaker (p$K_a$ well above 15), so D is the least acidic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Number of molecules from below which cannot give iodoform reaction is:
Ethanol, Isopropyl alcohol, Bromoacetone, 2-Butanol, 2-Butanone, Butanal, 2-Pentanone, 3-Pentanone, Pentanal and 3-Pentanol.
questions.sol:
The test needs a $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ group or a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$ group (oxidised to it).
Positive: ethanol, isopropyl alcohol, bromoacetone ($\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2Br}$), 2-butanol, 2-butanone, 2-pentanone.
Negative: butanal, 3-pentanone, pentanal, 3-pentanol: 4.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In the following reactions, which one is NOT correct?
questions.sol:
Ethanol, like $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$, reduces a diazonium salt to the arene (benzene), with ethanol oxidised to ethanal; it does not give ethoxybenzene. So reaction (1) is wrong.
(2) $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ gives benzene, (3) CuCN/KCN gives benzonitrile and (4) KI gives iodobenzene: all correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct structure of L-Fructose?
questions.sol:
D-Fructose (Fischer projection, C2 = C=O): C3-OH on the left, C4-OH and C5-OH on the right.
L-Fructose is its mirror image: C3-OH on the right, C4-OH and C5-OH on the left, which is structure (2).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given :
$\Delta H^\ominus_{\text{sub}}$ [C (graphite)] = 710 kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\Delta_{\mathrm{C-H}}H^\ominus$ = 414 kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\Delta_{\mathrm{H-H}}H^\ominus$ = 436 kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\Delta_{\mathrm{C=C}}H^\ominus$ = 611 kJ mol$^{-1}$
The $\Delta H_f^\ominus$ for $\mathrm{CH_2=CH_2}$ is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (nearest integer value)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{2C(graphite)+2H_2(g)\rightarrow C_2H_4(g)}$.
Energy in: $2\times710+2\times436=2292$ kJ. Energy out (bonds formed): $4\times414+611=2267$ kJ.
$\Delta H_f^\ominus=2292-2267=25$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The number of optical isomers exhibited by the iron complex (A) obtained from the following reaction is __________.
$\mathrm{FeCl_3+KOH+H_2C_2O_4\rightarrow A}$
questions.sol:
A is $\mathrm{K_3[Fe(C_2O_4)_3]}$, an octahedral complex with three bidentate oxalate ligands, $[\mathrm{M(AA)_3}]$.
It is chiral and exists as two enantiomers ($\Delta$ and $\Lambda$): 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions
$\mathrm{A+\underset{\text{Little amount}}{NaCl}+H_2SO_4\rightarrow CrO_2Cl_2}$ + Side Products
$\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ (Vapour) + NaOH $\rightarrow$ B + NaCl + $\mathrm{H_2O}$
B + $\mathrm{H^+}$ $\rightarrow$ C + $\mathrm{H_2O}$
The number of terminal 'O' present in the compound 'C' is __________.
questions.sol:
This is the chromyl chloride test: A is a dichromate; $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}$ with NaOH gives sodium chromate, B $=\mathrm{Na_2CrO_4}$.
Acidifying chromate gives dichromate, C $=\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7}$ ($\mathrm{2CrO_4^{2-}+2H^+\rightarrow Cr_2O_7^{2-}+H_2O}$).
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ has one bridging O and $2\times3=6$ terminal O.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
0.5 g of an organic compound on combustion gave 1.46 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and 0.9 g of $\mathrm{H_2O}$. The percentage of carbon in the compound is __________. (Nearest integer)
[Given : Molar mass (in g mol$^{-1}$) C : 12, H : 1, O : 16]
questions.sol:
Mass of C $=1.46\times\dfrac{12}{44}=0.398$ g.
Percentage $=\dfrac{0.398}{0.5}\times100\approx79.6\%$, i.e. 80.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
During estimation of nitrogen by Dumas' method of compound X (0.42 g)
__________ mL of $\mathrm{N_2}$ gas will be liberated at STP. (nearest integer)
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ : C : 12, H : 1, N : 14)
questions.sol:
X is piperazine, $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}N_2}$, molar mass 86 g mol$^{-1}$; each molecule gives one $\mathrm{N_2}$.
Moles of $\mathrm{N_2}=\dfrac{0.42}{86}=4.88\times10^{-3}$.
Volume at STP $=4.88\times10^{-3}\times22400\approx109$ mL.
